newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia to invest $3.9bln in projects by 2000-paper.
newsitem.headline: Serbia to invest $3.9bln in projects by 2000-paper.

text.p: Serbia plans to spend $3.9 billion and over 4.6 billion dinars by the year 2000 in infrastructure development projects, Belgrade dailies reported on Wednesday.
"Serbia plans to invest $2.63 billion in its power industry and $1.25 in its oil industry," Deputy President of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce Momir Pavlicevic was quoted by daily Borba as saying.
It will set out 853.4 million dinars ($149 million) for development of Serbia's railways and 160 million dinars for roads.
Another 2.6 billion dinars are earmarked for the development of post and telecommunications this year.

Telecommunications will be developed in two stages -- in the first, serbia plans to spend 822 million dinars to complete all investment projects started in 1996. In the second, around 1.8 billion dinars will be invested in development activities.
The plan is to install 530,985 new telephone lines.
He said the projects have to be financed from real sources, regular revenue of public firms, sale of oil derivatives, sales tax, the Development Fund, foreign credits and concessions.

Telecommunications, road and electricity industries are most attractive to investors and most likely to secure foreign capital through concessions, Pavlicevic said. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
